extracted.intended_audience: Researchers (emerging and established) applying to SSHRC Insight Development Grants (February 2026 competition), and institutional research offices supporting applicants
extracted.subtask_description: Prepare and submit an application to the Social Sciences and Humanities Research Council (SSHRC) Insight Development Grants February 2026 competition, meeting eligibility, budget, and merit-review expectations. The page defines eligibility, application procedures, merit review criteria, scoring, and rules for use of funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Challenge — The aim and importance of the endeavour (50%)
rubrics_metrics.description: Challenge—The aim and importance of the endeavour (50%):
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For established scholars: the proposal’s relevance to the objectives of the funding opportunity; originality, significance and expected contribution to knowledge; appropriateness of the literature review; appropriateness of the theoretical approach or framework; appropriateness of the methods/approach; quality of training and mentoring to be provided to students, emerging scholars and other highly qualified personnel, and opportunities for them to contribute; and potential for the project results to have influence and impact within and/or beyond the social sciences and humanities research community. (Weight: 50%)

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasibility — The plan to achieve excellence (20%)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes appropriateness of the proposed timeline and probability that the objectives will be met; expertise of the applicant or team in relation to the proposed research; appropriateness of the requested budget, justification of proposed costs, and, where applicable, other financial and/or in-kind contributions; and quality and appropriateness of knowledge mobilization plans, including for effective dissemination, exchange and engagement with stakeholders within and/or beyond the research community, where applicable. (Weight: 20%)

rubrics_metrics.name: Capability — The expertise to succeed (30%)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes quality, quantity and significance of past experience and published and/or creative outputs of the applicant and any co-applicants, relative to their roles in the project and the stage of their career; evidence of past knowledge mobilization activities (e.g., films, performances, commissioned reports, knowledge syntheses, experience in collaboration / other interactions with stakeholders, contributions to public debate and media), and of impacts on professional practice, social services and policies, etc.; and quality and quantity of past contributions to the development of effective research training and mentoring of students, postdoctoral researchers and other highly qualified personnel. Merit reviewers will consider information on only the last six years of research contributions; any career interruptions will be taken into consideration. (Weight: 30%)

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring scheme and funding threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Merit review scoring: scores range 1.00 (highest) to 6.00 (lowest) and are mapped to descriptors (1.00–1.83 Excellent; 1.84–2.67 Very good; 2.68–3.50 Good; 3.51–4.33 Satisfactory; 4.34–5.16 Moderate; 5.17–6.00 Unsatisfactory).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee members assign a score for each of the three criteria, apply the appropriate weighting to arrive at a final score. Applications must receive a score in the 'Moderate' range (i.e., 5.16–4.34) or better for each of the three criteria to be recommended for funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit review process characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Insight Development Grant applications are evaluated through a single-stage committee review process that does not involve external assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding decisions are based on committee recommendations and available funds. Committee discussions are guided by the principle of minimum essential funding. Merit review committees include national and international scholars and may include experts from other sectors. Normally, applications in the established stream that rank in the lowest 30% by committee consensus are not discussed during the final stage of merit review. SSHRC provides reviewers with Guidelines for the Merit Review of Indigenous Research to assist interpretation when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee selection and assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants will be asked to select the committee they consider most appropriate for review: discipline-based, groups of disciplines, multi/interdisciplinary (one humanities-focused and one social sciences-focused, plus Tri-Agency Interdisciplinary Peer Review Committee), or thematic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SSHRC will strive to accommodate preferences but reserves the right to determine an application’s review process and committee assignment. Applications spanning mandates of multiple federal agencies may select the Tri-Agency Interdisciplinary Peer Review Committee, which uses harmonized tri-agency criteria and requires that the dominant component is social sciences and humanities research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject-matter eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals can involve any disciplines, thematic areas, approaches or subject areas eligible for SSHRC funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications that would be more appropriately evaluated by NSERC or CIHR will not be accepted. Projects whose primary objective is curriculum development, preparation of teaching materials, program evaluation, organization of a conference or workshop, digitization of a collection or creation of a database are not eligible under this funding opportunity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget ineligibility threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: An application will be declared ineligible if it is determined that 30% or more of the requested budget has been allocated to non-eligible expenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should ensure budgets exclude non-eligible expenditures or keep them below the 30% threshold to avoid ineligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant affiliation and eligibility requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants (except postdoctoral fellows and PhD students) must be affiliated with a Canadian institution that holds institutional eligibility at the time of application and before funding can be released.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers whose primary affiliation is with a non-Canadian postsecondary institution are not eligible for applicant status. Applicants who have failed to submit a required achievement report by the deadline are ineligible to apply for another SSHRC grant until they have submitted the report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postdoctoral fellows and PhD candidate applicant conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Postdoctoral fellows are eligible to be applicants; eligible PhD candidates may apply only if they have met all PhD requirements before the grant is awarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For SSHRC to release funds, successful postdoctoral or eligible PhD applicants must formally establish an affiliation with an eligible Canadian postsecondary institution within three months of the grant start date and maintain such an affiliation for the duration of the grant. Eligible PhD students and postdoctoral fellows are encouraged to consult the Research Grants Office early.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional eligibility to administer funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Only eligible Canadian postsecondary institutions can administer grant funds awarded under this funding opportunity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions must meet institutional eligibility requirements independently of the application process and are encouraged to contact SSHRC’s Institutional Eligibility team at least 10 business days before the application deadline if seeking eligibility or with questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-applicants eligibility and replacement rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals (including postdoctoral fellows) are eligible to be co-applicants if they are formally affiliated with eligible Canadian postsecondary institutions or international postsecondary institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When international co-applicants are included, the application must clearly outline the rationale for international collaboration. Only a person named as a co-applicant in the original application can replace an applicant (principal investigator); any such replacement is subject to program approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborators — definition and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Any individual who makes a significant contribution to the project is eligible to be a collaborator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collaborators do not need to be affiliated with an eligible Canadian postsecondary institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple applications and interactions with Insight Grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals can apply as an applicant for only one Insight Development Grant at a time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normally researchers cannot apply as an applicant for an Insight Grant and an Insight Development Grant in the same calendar year, though SSHRC has allowed exceptions (e.g., unsuccessful Insight Development applicants in February may apply for an Insight Grant in October of the same year). Researchers who applied for an Insight Grant in October 2025 could apply for an Insight Development Grant in February 2026 if the objectives are significantly different. See SSHRC regulations on multiple applications for more details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring, reporting and post-award obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Grant holders will be expected to report on the use of grant funds, funded activities undertaken during the grant period, and outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful applicants will be informed of reporting requirements when they receive their notice of award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific rules for the use of grant funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Grant funds cannot be used to remunerate team members regardless of eligibility to apply for grants (including postdoctoral fellows serving as team members).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: in some cases Indigenous team members may be compensated per Tri-agency guideline on remuneration for Indigenous people participating in funded projects (with restrictions: team member may not be delegated to authorize grant expenditures and applicant/project director cannot be compensated). Additional prohibitions: funds cannot be used for remuneration and/or travel and subsistence costs of presenters or guest speakers, nor for course release time to allow an individual to engage in research activities. Permitted uses: consulting fees for expert/professional/technical services that contribute directly to proposed research (provided the service is not provided by a team member or by an individual whose status would make them eligible to hold a SSHRC grant). Grant funds can be used for travel and subsistence costs of collaborators related to research planning, exchange of information, and dissemination of results, but cannot be used for collaborators’ research costs to conduct research or research-related activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competition-specific fund allocation for emerging scholars
rubrics_metrics.description: For the current competition, at least 50% of funds will be reserved for applications from emerging scholars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should be aware of this allocation when considering competitiveness and eligibility streams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indigenous research review guidance and possible tailored review
rubrics_metrics.description: SSHRC’s Guidelines for the Merit Review of Indigenous Research are provided to reviewers to help build understanding and assist interpretation of evaluation criteria for Indigenous research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If SSHRC receives enough Indigenous research applications, it may establish a distinct merit review committee. SSHRC relies on reviewers experienced in Indigenous research to judge applicability of the guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference guidance and supporting documents applicants must consult
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are directed to consult SSHRC guidance documents when preparing applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key documents include SSHRC’s Definitions of Terms; Guidelines for Effective Research Training; Indigenous Research Statement of Principles and Guidelines for the Merit Review of Indigenous Research; definition of knowledge mobilization and Guidelines for Effective Knowledge Mobilization; Guidelines for Support of Tools for Research and Related Activities; Guidelines for Cash and In-Kind Contributions; and Preparing an application involving research-creation for Insight Grants and Insight Development Grants. Applicants should follow application form and accompanying application instructions and complete the Canadian Common CV per instructions.
